drafted_from: tool:read-what-shipped row (tools/export-records-as-list-rows/tool-rows.json), do-work/read_what_shipped.py, read-data/what_shipped.py and test/test_what_shipped.py; the answers are what the script printed on a made-up git repository with fixed commit dates
start_here: Say to your AI: "Read what my shop repository shipped since the last time and stage the new release in staged-releases.json, then tell me the newest entry."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it only stages each new release or commit as an entry in a file, which your mapping later turns into rows.
instructions: 1. Write ship-settings.json with mark (a git ref such as {"ref":"refs/heads/main"}, or a command that prints JSON), most_subjects and an optional id_prefix; add each "commit" and after to make every commit an entry.
2. Say "Read what shipped"; your AI reads the row with tools:list and runs its command from the Workshop checkout with {settings}, {repository} and {staged}.
3. Read releases (entries held), added (the newest entry added, or null when nothing was new) and added_count; run it again after more commits to add only the new ones.
4. Turn the staged file into list rows with your mapping and tool:export-records-as-list-rows.

worked_examples.title: The newest release of a shop repository is staged once
worked_examples.ask: Read what my shop repository shipped and stage it.
worked_examples.given: Read from a real run of do-work/read_what_shipped.py on a made-up repository with three commits on main (Rye on Sundays, Lemon tarts, A second van; the newest is 885c1b54cfb387771ff0dad0188b59437168fc02 dated 2026-03-03T08:00:00Z). The AI runs: python3 -I tools/export-records-as-list-rows/do-work/read_what_shipped.py --settings ship-settings.json --repository shop --staged staged-releases.json. ship-settings.json is {"mark":{"ref":"refs/heads/main"},"most_subjects":5,"id_prefix":"shop-"}. With no earlier release the entry holds the released commit's own subject alone.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"releases": 1, "added": "885c1b54cfb3", "added_count": 1}, exit 0. staged-releases.json holds one release: {"id": "shop-885c1b54cfb3", "name": "885c1b54cfb3", "commit": "885c1b54cfb387771ff0dad0188b59437168fc02", "at": "2026-03-03T08:00:00Z", "previous": null, "subjects": ["A second van"]}. After one more commit (Pie on Fridays) the same command prints {"releases": 2, "added": "565087d14d42", "added_count": 1}.
